newsitem.title: USA: Ill. agency okays COPs issue for school district.
newsitem.headline: Ill. agency okays COPs issue for school district.

text.p: The Illinois Development Finance Authority gave final approval Wednesday to the issuance of $55 million of certificates of participation for a financially troubled school district.

The unanimous approval by the board gave the go ahead for the Rockford School District to proceed to market. However, Linda Bobert, a senior vice president at Banc One Capital Corp, the underwriter for the COPs, said that talks were still ongoing with Financial Security Assurance on insuring the deal.
She added that the rating agencies were also taking a look at the deal and that the COPs would not be sold until March at the earliest.

The deal marks the first COPs issue for the development finance authority, which was brought into the deal because of its power to intercept state aid payments -- a requirement for obtaining insurance.

Under the deal's structure, the COPs would be a general obligation of the school district secured by a lien against property tax receipts. Those receipts would flow directly from the Winnebago County collector's office to an escrow held by a trustee.

Because the development finance authority has exhausted its state authorization to issue local government bonds, the COPs would be ultimately issued by a grantor trust. The agency's intercept powers would come into play should the school district's property tax collections prove insufficient.

The deficit-plagued Rockford School District is under a federal court order to sell the COPs to comply with another court order in an ongoing desegregation case that requires the district to build three new schools.

The state bonding authority also gave preliminary approval to the issuance of $157.7 million of taxable and tax-exempt 501(c)3 hospital acquisition bonds for Adventist Health System Sunbelt Healthcare Corp.

The deal, which is expected to be insured by AMBAC Indemnity Corp, would be underwritten by Ziegler Securities. Proceeds from the bond issue would be used to acquire the primary Illinois assets of Hinsdale Health System Inc.
